resources.string: Calibration patterns, manufacturer menus and input shortcuts
Offline SDR patterns use the highest supported output up to 4K. Your TV may still scale the image; check the pixel stripes. Left/Right changes patterns, OK shows or hides guidance, Back exits.
Fine black/white stripes should stay distinct. Reduce sharpening halos. If stripes merge, the display or Android may be scaling the surface.
White: outer edge. Green: 2.5% inset. Cyan: 5% inset. All edges should be visible and the circle should be round.
Full-range SDR values 0–24. Look for separation above black without raising the black background. These are RGB UI values, not video limited-range PLUGE.
Full-range SDR values 231–255. Look for visible differences near white without tinting the whites. Use a video clip to test video clipping.
Steps should look neutral and distinct; the lower gradient should be smooth. This SDR surface does not measure HDR brightness or color accuracy.
Full-intensity RGB color bars. Inspect tint and color uniformity; accurate color calibration requires a meter and suitable reference video.
The bar advances at the chosen cadence. Uneven motion can reveal frame pacing or display refresh mismatch. This tests Android drawing; use encoded motion clips to test video playback.
Left/Right: pattern · OK: guidance · Back: exit

Included HDR10 and Dolby Vision patterns work offline. You can also choose SDR, HDR10 or Dolby Vision test videos from USB or a document provider. Clips loop silently, without player enhancements or watch history. Selected file access stays on this device and is excluded from portable backups. Dolby Vision requires a compatible display, decoder and file profile.
Original video · looping · muted · OK: guidance · Back: exit
